⇒ 0.5 = 35

questions.question: Certain fielding restrictions in cricket during few overs are known as _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Power Play**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term **Power Play** refers to a set of fielding restrictions in cricket during certain overs of a match.
 
• In **One Day Internationals (ODIs)**, the first 10 overs of an innings are usually designated as power play overs, where only two fielders are allowed outside the 30-yard circle.
 
• In **T20 cricket**, the power play usually lasts for the first 6 overs, with similar fielding restrictions as in ODIs.
 
• The concept of power play is designed to create a balance between bat and ball, encouraging aggressive batting while giving bowlers a chance to take wickets with fewer fielders on the boundary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fielding Restrictions:**

 
 
• Fielding restrictions in cricket are rules that limit the placement of fielders in specific areas of the field during certain periods of the game.
 
• These restrictions are aimed at ensuring a balance between the batting and bowling teams, preventing defensive field placements throughout the innings.
 
• During the power play, the fielding team is restricted to having only a limited number of fielders outside the 30-yard circle.
 
 
 
• **30-Yard Circle:**
 
 
• The 30-yard circle is a fielding restriction area in cricket, marked by a circle with a 30-yard radius from each end of the pitch.
 
• It is used to enforce fielding restrictions, particularly during power plays, ensuring that only a certain number of fielders can be placed outside this area.
 
 
 
• **One Day Internationals (ODIs):**
 
 
• ODIs are a format of limited-overs cricket, where each team faces a fixed number of overs, usually 50.
 
• Power plays are an integral part of ODIs, with fielding restrictions varying at different stages of the innings.
 
 
 
• **T20 Cricket:**
 
 
• T20 cricket is a shorter format of the game, with each team playing a single innings of 20 overs.
 
• Power plays are more aggressive in T20s, lasting for the first 6 overs, encouraging explosive batting from the outset.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Bombay High Court of India established?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1862**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bombay High Court, one of the oldest High Courts in India, was established on **August 14, 1862**.
 
• It was established under the **Indian High Courts Act of 1861** by Queen Victoria.
 
• The jurisdiction of the Bombay High Court extends to the states of Maharashtra, Goa, and the Union Territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.
 
• The court has its principal seat in Mumbai (Bombay) and benches at Nagpur, Aurangabad, and Panaji (Goa).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian High Courts Act of 1861**

 
 
• The Indian High Courts Act of 1861 was an Act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom to establish High Courts in India.
 
• The Act authorized the British Crown to establish High Courts in the presidencies of Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras.
 
• The Act abolished the Supreme Courts at Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay and the Sadar Adalats in Presidency towns, merging their jurisdictions to form the High Courts.
 
• The High Courts were given the power to exercise original and appellate jurisdiction in civil and criminal cases.
 
 
 
• **Bombay High Court**
 
 
• The Bombay High Court is renowned for its rich heritage and historical significance.
 
• It has played a pivotal role in the development of Indian jurisprudence and has a long-standing tradition of delivering landmark judgments.
 
• The architectural design of the court building is a blend of Gothic and early English styles, symbolizing the legacy of British colonial rule in India.
 
• Prominent judges and lawyers, including Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and Nani Palkhivala, have been associated with the Bombay High Court.
 
 
 
• **Judicial System in India**
 
 
• The judicial system in India is a hierarchical system with the Supreme Court at the top, followed by High Courts at the state level, and subordinate courts at the district and lower levels.
 
• High Courts have the power to hear appeals from lower courts and have original jurisdiction in certain matters.
 
• The Indian judiciary is independent of the executive and legislative branches of government, ensuring the rule of law and protection of fundamental rights.
 
• Judicial review is a key function of the judiciary, allowing courts to examine the constitutionality of legislative and executive actions.

questions.question: Various Industrialists came together in 1944 and drafted a joint proposal for setting up a planned economy in India. It is famously known as the _________ Plan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bombay Plan was a set of proposals for the economic development of India, put forward by eight leading industrialists in 1944.
 
• The key figures involved were J.R.D. Tata, G.D. Birla, Lala Shri Ram, Kasturbhai Lalbhai, Ardeshir Dalal, A.D. Shroff, and John Mathai.
 
• The plan emphasized the importance of a mixed economy with both public and private sectors playing significant roles in the economic development.
 
• It advocated for substantial government intervention in various aspects of the economy including infrastructure, healthcare, and education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bombay Plan**

 
 
• The Bombay Plan was drafted by notable Indian industrialists during the British colonial rule, aiming to outline a vision for the country's economic future post-independence.
 
• The plan proposed a significant role for the state in economic planning and development, including large-scale investments in infrastructure and social sectors.
 
• It suggested the establishment of a National Planning Commission to oversee the implementation of planned economic policies.
 
• The plan underscored the importance of achieving self-sufficiency in key industries and reducing dependence on foreign goods and technology.
 
 
 
• **Planned Economy**
 
 
• A planned economy is an economic system in which the government or central authority makes all decisions about the production and distribution of goods and services.
 
• The objective is to allocate resources efficiently to meet the needs of the population and achieve economic goals such as growth, equity, and stability.
 
• In a planned economy, the government typically controls key industries, sets prices, and determines the allocation of resources.
 
• This contrasts with a market economy, where decisions are driven by market forces such as supply and demand.

questions.question: India got its central bank in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1935**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established on **April 1, 1935**.
 
• It was set up based on the recommendations of the **Hilton Young Commission**.
 
• The RBI was initially headquartered in Calcutta but was permanently moved to **Mumbai in 1937**.
 
• It was originally privately owned but was **nationalized in 1949** after India's independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**

 
 
• It is the central bank of India, responsible for regulating the issue and supply of the Indian rupee and managing the country's main payment systems.
 
• The RBI also plays a key role in the development strategy of the Indian government.
 
• The bank's main functions include monetary policy regulation, foreign exchange management, financial supervision, and development of the financial infrastructure.
 
• The RBI also acts as the banker to the government and to all scheduled commercial banks in India.
 
 
 
• **Hilton Young Commission**
 
 
• Also known as the Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, it was established in 1926.
 
• The commission recommended the creation of a central bank in India to manage the currency and credit system and to ensure monetary stability.
 
• Its recommendations led to the establishment of the Reserve Bank of India in 1935.
 
 
 
• **Nationalization of the Reserve Bank of India**
 
 
• The RBI was nationalized on January 1, 1949, under the Reserve Bank (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948.
 
• This move was aimed at aligning the central bank's operations with the economic policy of the government of India.
 
• Nationalization meant that the ownership and control of the RBI passed from private shareholders to the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bihar has the highest population density in India as per the 2011 Census.
 
• The population density of Bihar is 1,106 persons per square kilometer, which is significantly higher than the national average of 382 persons per square kilometer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Density**

 
 
• Population density is a measurement of population per unit area or unit volume.
 
• It is often represented as people per square kilometer or people per square mile.
 
• This metric is used to understand the distribution of population in a specific area and is crucial for urban planning and resource allocation.
 
 
 
• **2011 Census**

• **Factors Affecting Population Density**
 
 
• Several factors influence population density, including geographical area, fertility rates, mortality rates, migration patterns, and government policies.
 
• Areas with favorable living conditions, job opportunities, and better infrastructure tend to have higher population densities.
 
• Conversely, regions with harsh climates, lack of resources, and limited economic opportunities typically have lower population densities.

• It can also result in increased competition for jobs, housing, and services.
 
• On the positive side, high population density can foster economic growth, cultural exchange, and innovation due to the concentration of people and activities.

__
 
• Praveen Kumar Srivastava was sworn in as the Central Vigilance Commissioner (CVC) in May 2023.
 
• The Central Vigilance Commission is an apex Indian governmental body created in 1964 to address governmental corruption.
 
• The CVC is an autonomous body, free of control from any executive authority, monitoring all vigilance activities under the Central Government.
 
• The appointment of the CVC is made by the President of India on the recommendation of a committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Home Minister, and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)**

 
 
• The Central Vigilance Commission was established in 1964 based on the recommendations of the Committee on Prevention of Corruption, headed by K. Santhanam.
 
• The role of the CVC is to monitor all vigilance activities under the Central Government and advise various authorities in central government organizations in planning, executing, reviewing, and reforming their vigilance work.
 
• The CVC is vested with the power to inquire into offenses alleged to have been committed under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, by certain categories of public servants.
 
• The CVC has three members: The Central Vigilance Commissioner and two Vigilance Commissioners. They are appointed by the President of India on the recommendation of a committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Minister of Home Affairs, and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of India (CJI)**
 
 
• The Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary of India and the Supreme Court of India.
 
• The CJI is responsible for the allocation of cases and appointment of constitutional benches, which deal with important matters of law.
 
• The CJI is appointed by the President of India and serves until the age of 65.
 
 
 
• **Vice President of India**
 
 
• The Vice President of India is the second-highest constitutional office in the country, after the President.
 
• The Vice President also serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• The Vice President is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both houses of Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Attorney-General for India**
 
 
• The Attorney-General for India is the chief legal advisor to the Government of India and its primary lawyer in the Supreme Court of India.
 
• The Attorney-General is appointed by the President of India under Article 76(1) of the Constitution and must be a person qualified to be appointed as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
 
• The Attorney-General has the right of audience in all courts in India as well as the right to participate in the proceedings of the Parliament, though not to vote.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Brahmo Samaj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Rammohun Roy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Raja Rammohun Roy was a prominent social reformer and is known as the father of the Indian Renaissance.
 
• He founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828 to fight against social evils like the caste system, child marriage, and Sati.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj played a significant role in the modernization of Indian society and promoted the values of rationalism, humanism, and monotheism.
 
• Raja Rammohun Roy was also instrumental in the abolition of Sati, a practice where widows were forced to self-immolate on their husbands' funeral pyres.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmo Samaj:**

 
 
• The Brahmo Samaj is a socio-religious reform movement in the Indian subcontinent, founded by Raja Rammohun Roy in 1828.
 
• It aimed to reform and modernize Hindu society by discarding practices like idol worship and promoting monotheism.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj emphasized the importance of reason, morality, and the worship of one God.
 
• It also focused on social reforms such as the abolition of the caste system, women's education, and the fight against child marriage and dowry.
 
 
 
• **Raja Rammohun Roy:**
 
 
• Raja Rammohun Roy (1772-1833) was a prominent Indian social reformer and the founder of the Brahmo Samaj.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Father of the Indian Renaissance" due to his efforts in bringing about social and educational reforms in India.
 
• Rammohun Roy was a strong advocate for women's rights and played a key role in the abolition of the practice of Sati.
 
• He also promoted the idea of Western education and was instrumental in the establishment of the Hindu College in Calcutta (now Kolkata).
 
 
 
• **Social Reforms:**
 
 
• The Brahmo Samaj was at the forefront of various social reforms in India, advocating for the abolition of practices such as Sati, child marriage, and the caste system.
 
• It promoted women's education and worked towards improving the status of women in society.
 
• The movement also encouraged the adoption of Western education and scientific thinking among Indians.
 
• Through its efforts, the Brahmo Samaj aimed to create a more just and equitable society based on the principles of reason, morality, and monotheism.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the ninth five-year plan of India?

I. The plan focused on growth with social justice and equality.

II. The time period of the ninth-five-year plan is 1997-2002.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

• The Ninth Five-Year Plan of India aimed at achieving growth with social justice and equality.
 
• The duration of the Ninth Five-Year Plan was from 1997 to 2002.
 
• This plan was launched after the economic reforms of the 1990s and was influenced by the economic liberalization policies introduced during that period.
 
• The plan emphasized the importance of sustainable development and the equitable distribution of resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans in India**

 
 
• India's Five-Year Plans were centralized and integrated national economic programs. They were modeled after the Soviet Union's planning system.
 
• The first such plan was launched in 1951, and the last (12th) plan was from 2012 to 2017.
 
• These plans aimed at economic growth, modernization, self-reliance, and social justice.
 
 
 
• **Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997-2002)**
 
 
• This plan was launched under the leadership of then Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
 
• It aimed to achieve a growth rate of 6.5% per annum.
 
• It focused on agriculture and rural development with a view to generate adequate employment and eradicate poverty.
 
• The plan also aimed at containing population growth, ensuring food and nutritional security, providing basic minimum services of safe drinking water, primary health care facilities, universal primary education, and shelter to all.
 
• Special attention was given to the empowerment of women and socially disadvantaged groups such as Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and Other Backward Classes (OBC).
 
 
 
• **Economic Liberalization**
 
 
• Economic liberalization in India refers to the economic reforms introduced in 1991.
 
• These reforms were aimed at opening up the Indian economy to global markets, reducing the control of the state over the economy, and encouraging private enterprise.
 
• The reforms included measures such as deregulation, reduction of import tariffs, and the removal of subsidies.

questions.question:
Read the following about the supply of Money.

A. In a modern economy, money comprises cash and bank deposits.

B. These are created by a system comprising two types of institutions: central bank of the economy and the commercial banking system.

Identify the CORRECT statement/statements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a modern economy, money supply includes both cash (currency) and bank deposits.
 
• The money supply is created by a combination of central banks and commercial banks.
 
• Cash refers to physical money in the form of coins and banknotes.
 
• Bank deposits are funds held in bank accounts, which can be accessed through various financial instruments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Money Supply**

 
 
• The money supply is the total amount of monetary assets available in an economy at a specific time.
 
• It includes physical currency, demand deposits, and other liquid assets.
 
• Central banks control the money supply through monetary policy to ensure economic stability.
 
 
 
• **Central Bank**
 
 
• The central bank is a national institution that manages the currency, money supply, and interest rates.
 
• Examples include the Federal Reserve in the USA, the European Central Bank in Europe, and the Reserve Bank of India in India.
 
• Central banks are responsible for regulating the banking industry and ensuring financial stability.
 
 
 
• **Commercial Banks**
 
 
• Commercial banks are financial institutions that provide banking services to individuals and businesses.
 
• They accept deposits, offer loans, and provide various financial services like savings accounts, checking accounts, and certificates of deposit.
 
• Commercial banks play a critical role in the money creation process by lending out deposits, which increases the money supply.

questions.question: 'Kuchipudi' classical dance form is associated with which of the following states?

__
 
• **Kuchipudi** is one of the eight major Indian classical dances.
 
• It originated in a village named **Kuchipudi** in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• This dance form is known for its **fast rhythms and fluid movements, creating a blend of grace and vigor.**
 
• Kuchipudi performances include a combination of **dance, acting, and music**, often telling stories from Hindu epics and mythology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classical Dance Forms of India:**

 
 
• **Bharatanatyam:** Originated in Tamil Nadu, it is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork combined with expressive hand gestures and facial expressions.
 
• **Kathak:** Originated in North India, it is characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures and is often performed as a narrative dance form telling stories.
 
 
• **Kuchipudi Dance Techniques:**
 
 
• **Tarangam:** A unique aspect of Kuchipudi where the dancer performs rhythmic patterns on the rim of a brass plate, often balancing a pot on the head.
 
• **Natya:** The dramatic aspect where the dancer enacts a story, often from Hindu epics, with expressive gestures and facial expressions.
 
• **Nritya:** The pure dance aspect focusing on intricate footwork and body movements without any narrative.

__
 
• The sex ratio in India as per the 2011 Census is **943 females per 1000 males**.
 
• This was an improvement from the 2001 Census where the sex ratio was 933 females per 1000 males.
 
• The sex ratio is an important social indicator to measure the extent of prevailing equity between males and females in a society at a given point in time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Sex Ratio**
 
 
• The sex ratio is the ratio of males to females in a population.
 
• It is expressed as the number of females per 1000 males.
 
• This demographic indicator helps understand the gender balance within a population.

questions.question: Haddu khan and Hassu Khan were regarded as great masters of which style?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khyal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Haddu Khan and Hassu Khan were celebrated maestros of the Khyal style of classical Indian music.
 
• Khyal is characterized by its flexibility and improvisation, allowing the artist to explore and express emotions deeply.
 
• Haddu Khan and Hassu Khan belonged to the Gwalior Gharana, which is one of the oldest and most prestigious gharanas of Khyal singing.
 
• Their contributions and mastery significantly influenced and enriched the development and popularity of Khyal music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dhrupad**

 
 
• Dhrupad is one of the oldest forms of North Indian classical music, known for its spiritual and meditative qualities.
 
• It is marked by a strict adherence to the raga's structure and a slow, deliberate tempo.
 
• Famous exponents of Dhrupad include the Dagar brothers and the Gundecha brothers.
 
 
 
• **Tappa**
 
 
• Tappa is a form of North Indian semi-classical music that originated from the folk songs of camel riders in Punjab.
 
• It is characterized by its intricate and rapid note patterns and distinctive rhythmic structure.
 
• Renowned Tappa singers include Shori Miyan and Girija Devi.
 
 
 
• **Thumri**
 
 
• Thumri is a genre of semi-classical Indian music known for its romantic and devotional themes.
 
• It emphasizes expressive and emotive singing, often focusing on the lyrics and their meaning.
 
• Notable Thumri singers include Begum Akhtar and Shobha Gurtu.
 
 
 
• **Khyal**
 
 
• Khyal is the most popular form of classical music in North India today, known for its improvisational nature.
 
• It allows for a wide range of creativity and expression, with a focus on vocal agility and emotional depth.
 
• Khyal performances often include elaborate and intricate improvisations on the raga.
 
• Famous Khyal singers include Ustad Amir Khan, Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, and Kishori Amonkar.

questions.question: __________ is the main festival of Karnataka, which marks the Kannada new year.

__
 
• **Ugadi** is celebrated as the Kannada New Year and is one of the most important festivals in Karnataka.
 
• It is observed on the first day of the Chaitra month in the Hindu lunisolar calendar, which usually falls in March or April.
 
• Ugadi signifies the beginning of a new era and is a time for people to clean their homes, prepare special dishes, and perform religious rituals to welcome the new year.
 
• Traditional foods such as "Bevu-Bella" (a mixture of neem and jaggery) are consumed to symbolize the acceptance of both bitter and sweet experiences in life.

• Vitappa is a deity and the festival associated with it, Sri Vitappa fair, is celebrated in the state of Karnataka, but it is not the Kannada New Year.
 
• This festival is specific to the worship of the deity Vitappa and includes fairs, processions, and various cultural activities.
 
 
 
• **Hampi**
 
 
• Hampi is a historic village in Karnataka, renowned for its ancient temples and ruins of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• While Hampi is a significant cultural and historical site, it is not related to the Kannada New Year celebration.
 
 
 
• **Basava Jayanti**
 
 
• Basava Jayanti is celebrated in honor of Basavanna, a philosopher and statesman who founded the Lingayat sect.
 
• This festival is important in Karnataka but does not mark the Kannada New Year.

questions.question: In the Indian subcontinent, the beginning of settlement at Mehrgarh started about __________ years ago.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8000**__ years ago.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mehrgarh is one of the earliest known settlements in the Indian subcontinent, dating back to around 8000 years ago.
 
• It is located in present-day Pakistan, in the Balochistan province.
 
• The settlement is significant for its early evidence of farming (wheat and barley) and herding (cattle, sheep, and goats).
 
• Mehrgarh is considered a precursor to the Indus Valley Civilization, showcasing early human advancements in agriculture and settlement patterns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mehrgarh**

 
 
• Mehrgarh is one of the most important Neolithic (7000 BCE to 2500 BCE) sites in South Asia, showing the development of early farming and pastoral societies.
 
• Archaeological evidence indicates the early use of pottery, tools, and domestication of animals.
 
• The site has provided crucial insights into the early stages of human settlement and the transition from nomadic to settled life.
 
• Excavations at Mehrgarh have revealed a rich cultural sequence, including burial practices, housing structures, and early craft activities.
 
 
 
• **Indus Valley Civilization**

questions.question: A person loses 30 percent on selling 54 chairs for Rs. 70. What should be the selling price of 54 chairs to earn a profit of 15 percent?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A person loses 30 percent on selling 54 chairs for Rs. 70.

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = Selling Price (SP) / (1 - Loss%)

Selling Price (SP) for 15% profit = CP × (1 + Profit%)

**Calculation:**

Selling Price (SP) for 54 chairs = Rs. 70

Loss% = 30%

Cost Price (CP) for 54 chairs:

⇒ CP = SP / (1 - Loss%)

⇒ CP = 70 / (1 - 0.30)

⇒ CP = 70 / 0.70

⇒ CP = 100

Profit% = 15%

Selling Price (SP) for 15% profit:

⇒ SP = CP × (1 + Profit%)

⇒ SP = 100 × (1 + 0.15)

⇒ SP = 100 × 1.15

⇒ SP = 115

**The selling price of 54 chairs to earn a profit of 15 percent is Rs. 115.**
